## Summary
Six replicas work for the stateless API, but the database is the limit: 60 pooled connections and the `$lastn` N+1. Availability of clinical data during flu season is patient-safety relevant, so connection exhaustion is rated critical.

## Findings
| id | severity | category | location | evidence | recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARC-001 | info | deployability | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/config/SecurityConfig.java:40 | `SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS` with HTTP Basic per request: the API is stateless, so no session affinity is needed | Scale horizontally as is. |
| ARC-002 | critical | performance | sample-app/src/main/resources/application.yml:5 | No `spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size`: the default Hikari connection pool of 10 per pod x 6 pods = 60 connections, plus surge pods during a rolling update, against PostgreSQL max_connections | Set the pool size explicitly (for example 5) or put PgBouncer in front of PostgreSQL. |
| ARC-003 | high | performance | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/service/ObservationService.java:69 | The known $lastn N+1 (`TEACHING-DEFECT(perf-n+1)`, 2 queries per subject) multiplies database load as replicas add throughput | Raise a separate, explicitly scoped ticket for it before the season. |
| ARC-004 | low | deployability | sample-app/k8s/deployment.yaml:13 | Fixed `replicas: 2`, no HPA or PodDisruptionBudget | Add a HorizontalPodAutoscaler on CPU and a PodDisruptionBudget with `minAvailable: 2`. |

## Decisions
- Scale with an HPA (min 2, max 6) after setting the pool size.
